entries.clue: When woe wants a word, the grieving on the old boards sigh out this one
Bluish-green, and the prefix on a gentle exercise class held in water
Forest heroine who woos in a young man's clothing
Royal regatta rowed two abreast on a straight stretch of the Thames
Floppy foam tube a learner straddles; also a strip of pasta
Wife smothered on the evidence of a mislaid handkerchief
Oar caught by the water at the finish, which can pitch a rower out
U-shaped fulcrum on the gunwale of a small wooden boat
Four and a quarter miles of Oxford against Cambridge each spring
Bring a tiring friend in on a line, as lifesavers are taught
Use it as the subject when speaking to one person; 'art' follows, not 'are'
Remark meant for the audience alone, unheard by others on the boards
Perish for want of air beneath the surface, as weak swimmers may
Flat oblong of foam held out in front while the feet do the work
